newsitem.title: UK: UK Internet ads seen reaching 4 pct of all adverts.
newsitem.headline: UK Internet ads seen reaching 4 pct of all adverts.

text.p: Companies in Britain spent an estimated 4.0 million stg on advertising on the Internet in 1996, NewMediaAge magazine reported on Friday.

The weekly magazine quoted a report by Dresdener Kleinwort Benson (DKB), the investment house, that predicted that Internet advertising's share of total advertising could rise from a current 0.4 percent to 2.0 percent by 2000.
The report, called "Going Digital", forecast the value of UK advertising on the Internet would reach 266 million stg by 2001.

The figures were was based on the expected number of Internet subscribers in Britain reaching 4.25 million by 2001 and on an 11-fold increase in the level of advertising expenditure per UK Internet user.

The magazine quoted DKB's Michael Hilton, who wrote the report, as saying the 4.0 million stg figure for 1996 was calculated by scaling down estimates of the global Internet advertising market in line with UK "traffic levels".

Hilton said the 2.0 percent forecast for 2001 was in contrast to a prediction by Jupiter Communications that ads placed on the Internet by companies in the United States would amount to 4.0 to 6.0 percent of the total U.S. advertising market by 2001.
Jupiter is a New York-based research, consulting and publishing company that specialises in consumer online and interactive technologies.
The DKB report said it was unlikely the UK market for Internet advertising would grow bigger than the forecast 4.0 percent of total advertising.
But Hilton said there was a lack of relevant statistics on Internet advertising in Britain.
